channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Serbia Establish Strategic Partnership, Boost Business Ties
item.description: Presidents Shavkat Mirziyoyev and Aleksandar Vučić attended a joint business forum, marking the establishment of a strategic partnership between Uzbekistan and Serbia. Over 200 business representatives participated, aiming to increase trade and industrial cooperation.

item.title: Belgrade Street Named 'Tashkent' to Symbolize Strong Uzbek-Serbian Relations
item.description: A street in Belgrade has been named 'Tashkent' during the official visit of Uzbekistan's President Shavkat Mirziyoyev to Serbia. This naming signifies the dynamic development of bilateral relations, now elevated to a strategic partnership, and symbolizes friendship between the two nations.

item.title: Uzbekistan to participate in 200km railway construction in Serbia
item.description: Uzbekistan's builders will participate in constructing a 200-kilometer railway in Serbia. Additionally, direct flights will be launched between Tashkent and Mauritius. A person promising a governor's position for $210,000 was arrested in Fergana. Uzbekistan ranked 48th out of 91 countries in natural sciences in PISA 2025.

item.title: Uzbek President Awarded Order of the Republic of Serbia
item.description: Uzbekistan's President Shavkat Mirziyoyev received Serbia's highest state honor, the Order of the Republic of Serbia on a Grand Chain. Serbian President Aleksandar Vučić presented the award in Belgrade, recognizing Mirziyoyev's significant contribution to strengthening Uzbek-Serbian relations.

item.title: Poverty Reduction Efforts Examined in Shumanay District
item.description: A press tour in Shumanay District, Karakalpakstan, showcased efforts to reduce poverty and increase incomes. A press conference detailed measures for 2026, including creating 6,877 jobs and developing local businesses based on regional advantages, aligning with state directives.

item.title: Uzbekistan-Serbia Trade Turnover Grows Significantly
item.description: Trade and economic ties between Uzbekistan and Serbia have strengthened, with turnover increasing nearly ninefold from $1.4 million to $12 million between 2016-2025. Both nations aim to reach $50 million in mutual trade soon.

item.title: Twelve countries ban trade with Israeli settlements amid rising violence
item.description: Twelve countries, including 11 European nations and Canada, have banned trade with Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank due to rising violence. In response, Israeli officials ordered the closure of the British consulate in Jerusalem. This action follows increased tensions and violence in the region.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Serbia Establish Strategic Partnership
item.description: Uzbekistan and Serbia signed a Joint Declaration establishing a strategic partnership following talks in Belgrade. Leaders witnessed the exchange of documents on cooperation in areas including labor migration, transport, agriculture, renewable energy, and ICT.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Serbia Establish New Diplomatic Relations Phase
item.description: Uzbekistan and Serbia have entered a new phase of diplomatic relations, marked by increased political dialogue and high-level meetings. Following a summit in Tashkent, leaders signed a joint statement to expand cooperation in political, economic, and cultural spheres. Agreements were signed to strengthen economic ties and establish new consultative mechanisms.

item.title: Uzbekistan Prosecutor General's Office receives appeal to preserve historic building
item.description: Uzbekistan's Agency for Cultural Heritage has appealed to the Prosecutor General's Office to preserve a historic building at 7 Bobur Street in Tashkent. The appeal questions the legality of a 2018 decision that allocated the land for demolition and construction.

item.title: Serbia expresses readiness to cooperate with Uzbekistan on ballistic missile production
item.description: Serbia has announced its willingness to collaborate with Uzbekistan in the production of ballistic missiles. The country is already manufacturing short-range missiles and could begin producing long-range ballistic missiles within a year.

item.title: New water intake facility completed on Ak-Buura River in Osh, Kyrgyzstan
item.description: Construction of a new water intake facility has been completed on the Ak-Buura River in the Dangi section of Osh, Kyrgyzstan. The project, funded by the Asian Development Bank and the Osh mayor's office, includes a new headworks and a 2,400-meter main pipeline to supply drinking water.

item.title: Central Asia-China Political Parties Dialogue Held in Samarkand
item.description: A conference on the role of political parties in strengthening ties between Central Asia and China took place in Samarkand. The forum aimed to enhance inter-party dialogue, support interstate agreements, and achieve economic and social results. Representatives from Central Asian nations and China participated.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Armenia Discuss Bilateral Cooperation Prospects
item.description: Uzbekistan and Armenia held political consultations in Yerevan to discuss cooperation in political, trade-economic, and cultural-humanitarian spheres. Both sides expressed interest in expanding the legal framework and strengthening interaction on international platforms, focusing on industrial cooperation and transport.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan aims to export beans to Pakistan, boosting agricultural trade
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Minister of Water Resources, Agriculture, and Processing Industry met with Pakistan's Ambassador to discuss bean exports. The focus is on establishing direct links between producers and importers, participating in trade shows, and agreeing on supply volumes and terms. Kyrgyzstan's bean export potential exceeds 50,000 tons annually.

item.title: First Uzbek-Serbian Intergovernmental Commission Meeting Held in Belgrade
item.description: The first meeting of the Uzbek-Serbian Intergovernmental Commission on Economic Cooperation convened in Belgrade. Discussions focused on strengthening partnership, liberalizing trade, and establishing a working group for a free trade agreement. Cooperation in localization, textiles, and agriculture was also explored.

item.title: Uzbek President proposes five cooperation areas for joint projects with Serbia
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev outlined five priority areas for economic cooperation with Serbia: mechanical engineering and electrical engineering, pharmaceuticals, light industry, agriculture, and the digital economy. He emphasized translating political agreements into practical implementation through joint production and investments.

item.title: Kazakh language Latin script transition lacks specific timeline
item.description: There are no concrete deadlines for the Kazakh language's transition to the Latin script. Specialists are refining the new alphabet and orthography rules. The Ministry of Science and Higher Education stated that until official approval, using Latin script variants is premature. The transition has been discussed since 2012, with a 2017 decree aiming for completion by 2025, but timelines were later revised.

item.title: Uzbekistan enhances transparency mechanisms in public procurement
item.description: Uzbekistan is improving transparency, accountability, and control in public procurement to ensure rational use of budget funds. A draft law discussed in the Legislative Chamber proposes publishing procurement data by region and strengthening parliamentary oversight. It also suggests establishing territorial units to expedite complaint resolution for entrepreneurs.

item.title: Serbia offers cooperation with Uzbekistan on ballistic missiles
item.description: Serbia has expressed readiness to cooperate with Uzbekistan in the defense industry, specifically on long-range ballistic missiles. Serbian President Aleksandar Vučić announced this at a business forum in Belgrade. He stated that relations between the two countries have reached their highest point in modern history, with a strategic partnership now established.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Serbia presidents attend joint business forum, sign agreements
item.description: The presidents of Uzbekistan and Serbia participated in a joint business forum, where Shavkat Mirziyoyev outlined priority areas for further economic partnership. Several bilateral economic agreements and trade contracts were signed during the event. The leaders also discussed establishing a direct flight route between Belgrade and Tashkent.

item.title: Serbia considers free trade agreement with Uzbekistan
item.description: During the Uzbek President's visit to Serbia, an intergovernmental commission meeting discussed economic cooperation. Serbia's Minister of International Economic Relations, Nenad Popović, stated that a free trade agreement between the two countries is being considered. He highlighted complementary economies and potential in new technologies.

item.title: Belgrade Street to Be Named "Tashkent"
item.description: A street in Belgrade will be named "Tashkent" in a ceremony attended by Uzbekistan's President Shavkat Mirziyoyev during his official visit to Serbia. Serbian President Aleksandar Vučić stated that Tashkent, a city rich in history and modern development, will now hold a special place in the Serbian capital.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Aims to Reduce Food Import Dependence by 2030
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's government is working to decrease reliance on imported food products by 2030. While domestic production meets demand for potatoes, vegetables, and milk, shortfalls exist for meat, eggs, sugar, and vegetable oil. Plans include increasing production of insufficient goods, improving storage and processing, and expanding cultivation of key crops.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Aims to Reduce Food Import Dependence by 2030
item.description: Kyrgyzstan plans to reduce its reliance on imported food products by 2030. While domestic production covers 100% of potatoes and vegetables, deficits exist for meat, eggs, sugar, vegetable oil, bread, and fruits. Efforts will focus on increasing production of insufficient goods and improving storage and processing.

item.title: Uzbekistan Building Second Nuclear Power Plant with China, President Vučić Reports
item.description: Uzbekistan is simultaneously developing two nuclear power projects, one with Russia and another with China, according to Serbian President Aleksandar Vučić. He stated that President Mirziyoyev informed him of this during a private meeting in Belgrade, emphasizing Uzbekistan's focus on future energy needs for data centers and AI.

item.title: Uzbekistan proposes lowering judicial age requirement from 35 to 30 years
item.description: A draft law reviewed in Uzbekistan's parliament proposes reducing the minimum age for judges and lay assessors from 35 to 30. The bill, developed by the Supreme Court, also revises appointment procedures, moving from multi-stage terms to a five-year initial term followed by a lifetime appointment. It aims to strengthen judicial independence and includes provisions for judges' social protection and the introduction of retired judges.

item.title: Ayaz Baetov Appointed Kyrgyzstan's Permanent Representative to the UN
item.description: Ayaz Baetov has been appointed Kyrgyzstan's Permanent Representative to the United Nations in New York. He replaces Aida Kasymalieva, who was transferred to another position. Baetov was previously relieved of his duties as Minister of Justice for a similar reason.

item.title: Ayaz Baetov Appointed Kyrgyzstan’s Permanent Representative to UN
item.description: Ayaz Baetov has been appointed as Kyrgyzstan's Permanent Representative to the UN in New York, replacing Aida Kasymalieva. Baetov was previously relieved of his duties as Justice Minister. Almaz Aiylchiev has been appointed Acting Justice Minister pending parliamentary approval.

item.title: Uzbekistan ranks 37th in Global Peace Index, leading Central Asia
item.description: Uzbekistan has climbed to 37th place out of 163 countries in the Global Peace Index 2026, according to the Institute for Economics and Peace. This marks a significant jump of 30 positions from the previous year. The nation achieved the highest ranking among Central Asian states, surpassing Kazakhstan, Tajikistan, Kyrgyzstan, and Turkmenistan, highlighting its image as a peaceful and stable country.

item.title: Zhyrgalbek Medetkanov Appointed Deputy Minister of Construction in Kyrgyzstan
item.description: Zhyrgalbek Medetkanov has been appointed Deputy Minister of Construction, Architecture, Housing, and Communal Services of Kyrgyzstan. He replaces Talantbek Imanakun uulu. Medetkanov previously headed the Department of Housing and Civil Construction and has worked in the construction industry since 2008.

item.title: New Deputy Minister of Construction Appointed in Kyrgyzstan
item.description: Zhyrgalbek Medetkanov has been appointed Deputy Minister of Construction, Architecture, Housing and Communal Services of Kyrgyzstan. The appointment was announced by the ministry and signed by the Chairman of the Cabinet of Ministers. Medetkanov replaces Talantbek Imanakun uulu, whose reasons for dismissal were not specified.

item.title: Uzbekistan to enhance state control in industrial, radiation, and nuclear safety
item.description: Uzbekistan's Legislative Chamber is considering amendments to improve state control over industrial, radiation, and nuclear safety. The proposed changes aim to refine the system of state oversight, clarify the powers of competent authorities, and introduce administrative responsibility for violations in the use of atomic energy. Financial sanctions for legal entities are also being reviewed to ensure compliance.

item.title: Naryn prepares for winter: 42 high-voltage substations repaired
item.description: The Naryn electricity network enterprise has repaired 42 out of 59 planned high-voltage substations. Specialists serviced a 40 MW transformer at the 'Naryn-1' substation, addressing oil leaks and conducting technical tests. Flood control measures are also underway.

item.title: Naryn Prepares for Winter: 42 High-Voltage Substations Repaired
item.description: The Naryn electricity network enterprise has repaired 42 out of 59 planned high-voltage substations. Specialists serviced a 40 MW power transformer at the 'Naryn-1' substation, addressing an oil leak and conducting technical tests. Flood protection measures are also planned for another facility, with work proceeding on schedule.

item.title: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev awarded Order of the Republic of Serbia
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev was awarded the Order of the Republic of Serbia in Belgrade. Serbian President Aleksandar Vučić presented the award for Mirziyoyev's significant contribution to strengthening multifaceted relations between Uzbekistan and Serbia.

item.title: Uzbekistan Cancels 1.5 Trillion Som Tax Penalties for 315,000 Entrepreneurs
item.description: Uzbekistan will waive tax penalties totaling 1.5 trillion som for nearly 315,000 entrepreneurs. This economic amnesty allows businesses that fully repay their tax debt by year-end to have accrued penalties discharged. The initiative stems from a presidential decree following a dialogue with entrepreneurs.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Serbia Establish Strategic Partnership Relations
item.description: Uzbekistan and Serbia have signed a joint declaration establishing strategic partnership relations. Presidents Shavkat Mirziyoyev and Aleksandar Vučić signed the document in Belgrade. Several bilateral agreements were also exchanged, covering areas such as labor mobility, transport, agriculture, energy, and tourism.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Serbia Forge Strategic Partnership
item.description: Uzbekistan and Serbia have established strategic partnership relations, signing a joint declaration in Belgrade. Presidents Shavkat Mirziyoyev and Aleksandar Vučić inked the document. The leaders also exchanged agreements on various cooperation areas, including trade, transport, and agriculture.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Minister of Transport urges acceleration of Lenin Street repair in Naryn
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Minister of Transport, Talantbek Soltobaev, inspected road construction and repair works in Naryn, focusing on Lenin Street. He urged contractors to speed up the process, noting that while asphalt has been laid on most of the 9-kilometer stretch, finishing works like installing traffic lights and road markings are ongoing. Additional workers and equipment have been deployed.
